words.notes: Before a person it has no English equivalent: Veo a Ana (I see Ana). a + el = al.
el (masculine), la (feminine); plural los, las.

words.gloss: to be (who or what something is)
words.notes: Use ser for identity and lasting traits, estar for states and places. Preterite fui, fue, fueron are shared with ir (Fue un buen día = It was a good day; Fue a casa = He went home).
Object pronoun: lo (him, it), la (her, it), los and las (them).
Plural unos, unas means 'some'.
Without the accent, que means 'that'.
Also in se llama (is called) and in general statements: ¿Cómo se dice? (How do you say it?)
conmigo = with me, contigo = with you.

words.gloss: to be (how or where something is)
words.notes: Use estar for states and places, ser for identity.
With an accent, mí means 'me': para mí (for me).
With an accent, sí means 'yes'.
Often left out: soy = I am.
Without the accent, si means 'if'.
hay = there is, there are. With a past participle: he comido (I have eaten).
tener que = to have to. Also for age and feelings: tengo hambre (I'm hungry).
Without the accent, tu means 'your'.
ir a + verb = going to: voy a comer (I'm going to eat). vamos also means 'let's go'. fui and fue are also forms of ser (fue un buen día = it was a good day).
With an accent, cómo means 'how'. Como is also the yo form of comer: como pan (I eat bread).
Also before a noun: toda la semana (all week), todos mis amigos (all my friends).

words.gloss: to know (a fact); to know how to

words.notes: With an accent, tú means 'you'.
Indirect object: le (to him, to her), les (to them). Before lo or la it becomes se: se lo doy.
For a thing or idea with no noun after it. Before a noun use este, esta.
ahora mismo = right now.
Before an adjective it means 'a bit': algo cansado (a bit tired).
Before a masculine singular noun it becomes buen: un buen día. Alone, bueno means 'well' or 'OK'.
Without the accent, el means 'the'.
In questions it has an accent: ¿cuándo?
With no: No tengo nada (I don't have anything). De nada = you're welcome.
Without the accent, como means 'like' or 'as'.
Before a word that starts with o or ho it becomes u: siete u ocho.
ellas = they, them (all female).
Irregular: hago, hice, hecho. For weather and time: hace frío (it's cold), hace dos años (two years ago).
Plural veces. a veces = sometimes, otra vez = again, tal vez = maybe.
Older spelling: sólo. As an adjective, solo means 'alone': estoy solo.
¿Por qué? (two words, with an accent) = why?
Creo que sí = I think so. Creo que no = I don't think so.
For things near the person you talk to. Also alone: ¿Quieres ese? (Do you want that one?)
Polite 'you'. It takes the same verb form as él and ella: usted es. Written Ud.
At the end of a question: ¿verdad? (right?). de verdad = really.
en casa = at home. a casa = (to) home.
tan ... como = as ... as: tan alto como tú.
Without the accent, quien links two parts of a sentence: el chico con quien hablo.
For clock time use hora: ¿Qué hora es?
los dos = both.
After a verb it needs no: No lo vi nunca.
Without the accent, donde links two parts of a sentence: la casa donde vivo.
por favor = please.
Also an adverb: Te quiero mucho (I love you a lot).
Without the accent, mi means 'my'. con + mí = conmigo.
Lo siento = I'm sorry. sentirse = to feel (well, bad): me siento bien.
Feminine señora (madam, Mrs., lady). Written Sr. and Sra. before a name.
Comparative of bueno and bien. el mejor = the best. a lo mejor = maybe.
Irregular: digo, dije, dicho. ¿Cómo se dice ...? = How do you say ...?
con + ti = contigo.
Irregular: vi, visto. a ver = let's see. Nos vemos = see you.
Also said to a friend in surprise: ¡Hombre!
para siempre = forever.
hasta luego = see you later. hasta mañana = see you tomorrow.
ahí = there, near the person you talk to. allí = over there.
For age: Tengo veinte años (I'm twenty).
antes de = before: antes de comer.
ni ... ni = neither ... nor.
un poco = a little: un poco de agua.
Masculine, although it ends in -a: el día. Buenos días = good morning.
Before a masculine noun it becomes un: un libro.
Buenas noches = good evening, good night. esta noche = tonight.
Never with un: otro café (another coffee).
de acuerdo = OK, agreed. estar de acuerdo = to agree.
Also a form of trabajar: trabajo = I work.
nosotras when all are female. Often left out: somos = we are.
¿Qué te parece? = What do you think?
Singular in Spanish: la gente es (people are).
los padres = parents (or fathers).
¡Mira! = Look! Also to get attention: Mira, ... (Listen, ...).
yo mismo = myself. ahora mismo = right now.
After a verb it needs no: No veo a nadie (I don't see anybody).
ellas when all are female.
¿Qué tal? = How are you? / How was it? tal vez = maybe.

words.gloss: to happen; to pass; to spend (time)
words.notes: ¿Qué pasa? = What's happening? / What's wrong? ¡Pasa! = Come in!
fuera de = outside (of). ¡Fuera! = Get out!
después de = after: después de comer.
desde hace = for (a time): desde hace un año (for a year).
todo el mundo = everybody.
¡Claro! = Of course! As an adjective: clear, light (claro, clara).
As a noun, la mañana means 'the morning'. pasado mañana = the day after tomorrow.
mañana por la mañana = tomorrow morning.
In Spain, ¡Vale! = OK! ¿Cuánto vale? = How much is it? valer la pena = to be worth it.
en lugar de = instead of.
In questions it has an accent: ¿dónde?
¿Estás seguro? = Are you sure? Seguro que ... = I'm sure that ... As a noun: insurance.

words.gloss: to wait (for); to hope; to expect

words.notes: de nuevo = again.
hija = daughter. hijos = children (sons and daughters).
Telling time: las tres menos diez (ten to three). por lo menos = at least.
Informal: guy. ¿Qué tipo de ...? = What kind of ...?
A female friend is amiga.
Before a singular noun: gran, which often means 'great': un gran hombre.
It agrees with the thing you own: nuestra casa, nuestros hijos.
Hasta luego = see you later. desde luego = of course.
Masculine, although it ends in -a. mis papás = my parents (in Latin America).
Irregular: oigo, oyes, oyó. ¡Oye! = Hey! (to get attention).
Me gusta el café = I like coffee (coffee pleases me). For more than one thing: me gustan los perros.
en todas partes = everywhere. de mi parte = from me.
Opposite of bien. Before a masculine noun it is an adjective: un mal día (a bad day).
debería = should. Also to owe: te debo diez euros.
Same as todavía. Without the accent, aun means 'even'.
After a noun: un amigo mío (a friend of mine).
It never changes form. cada día = every day.
Used like gustar: No me importa (I don't care). ¿Te importa ...? = Do you mind ...?
tener razón = to be right: tienes razón (you're right).
Before a masculine singular noun: algún. algunos = some, a few.
tanto ... como = as much ... as. Also an adverb: No comas tanto (Don't eat so much).
¿En serio? = Really?
Irregular: vengo, vine. ¡Ven! = Come! ¡Venga! = Come on!
No tengo ni idea = I have no idea.
As a noun, la tarde means 'the afternoon, the evening'. más tarde = later.
Buenas tardes = good afternoon. por la tarde = in the afternoon.
Masculine, although it ends in -a: el problema. No hay problema = no problem.
¿Qué hora es? = What time is it? Es hora de ... = It's time to ...
Es cierto = it's true. por cierto = by the way.
In questions it has an accent: ¿quién?
Before a noun it agrees: demasiada gente (too many people).
Also a pet name: mi amor (my love, honey).
la policía = the police. el policía, la policía = a police officer.
In Latin America for every plural 'you'; in Spain only the formal one. It takes the same verb form as ellos: ustedes son.
chica = girl. chicos can mean a mixed group: kids, guys.
La cuenta, por favor = The bill, please. darse cuenta = to realize.
Same as aún. todavía no = not yet.
Irregular: salgo, ¡sal! salir con = to go out with, to date.
hermana = sister. hermanos = brothers, or brothers and sisters.
e changes to ie: pienso, piensas. pensar en = to think about.
Me duele la cabeza = I have a headache.
Before a noun: cualquier. Alone: cualquiera (anyone, any one).
de todas formas = anyway. estar en forma = to be fit.
mientras tanto = meanwhile.
al lado de = next to. por otro lado = on the other hand.
en ese caso = in that case. hacer caso = to pay attention, to listen.
Before a masculine singular noun: primer. Also an adverb: primero = first (of all).
Irregular: supongo. por supuesto = of course.
Very common at the start of a sentence: Pues no sé (Well, I don't know).
Always feminine, also for a man: Él es una buena persona.

words.gloss: to come back; to go back
words.notes: o changes to ue: vuelvo. Irregular: vuelto. volver a + verb = to do again: volvió a llamar.
Both spellings are correct.
Also a form of caminar: camino = I walk.
de ninguna manera = no way. de todas maneras = anyway.
Also the past participle of morir: ha muerto (he has died). muerto de hambre = starving.
Also an adverb: ¡Ven rápido! (Come quickly!)
¿Cuál es ...? often means 'What is ...?': ¿Cuál es tu nombre?
¡Ayuda! = Help! The verb is ayudar.
Stem change e → ie: entiendo, entiendes. ¿Entendido? = Got it?
dentro de = inside of; in (dentro de una hora = in an hour).
¿Qué significa...? = What does ... mean?
fin de semana = weekend.
Usually plural: juntos, juntas. junto a = next to.
niña = girl. niños = children.
¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon! In Spain also 'early'.
tía = aunt. In Spain, tío / tía is also slang for a guy / girl, or 'mate'.
¡Buena suerte! = Good luck! tener suerte = to be lucky.
Almost always in ni siquiera = not even.
¡Feliz cumpleaños! = Happy birthday!
Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántos años? ¿cuánta gente?
Object pronoun for vosotros, used in Spain. Latin America uses les / los.
dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing. Déjame = let me / leave me.
en realidad = actually.
Irregular: doy, di, dio. Dame = give me.
Also a term of endearment: ¡Corazón! = Sweetheart!
tener miedo = to be afraid.
jefa = female boss.
Feminine, but el agua (el before a stressed a-): el agua fría.
no es justo = it's not fair. As an adverb: justo ahora = right now.
esposa = wife. esposos = husband and wife.
Feminine although it ends in -o: la mano.
¡Ojo! = Watch out!
¡Adelante! = Come in! / Go ahead!
Stem change o → ue: encuentro, encuentra.
Before a masculine noun: ningún (ningún problema). When it comes after the verb, put no before the verb: No tengo ninguna pregunta.
¡Cuidado! = Careful! / Watch out! tener cuidado = to be careful.
Opposite: alto. As a preposition, bajo means 'under': bajo la mesa.
cerca de = near (to).
Also a noun: un viejo = an old man.
Before an adjective it means 'quite': bastante bien = quite well.
por fin = finally. fin de semana = weekend.
¿Qué vas a tomar? = What will you have (to drink)? Toma = here you go.
lo único = the only thing.
Escucha = listen (command). Takes a direct object: escuchar música.
en punto = on the dot (a las tres en punto).
With an accent in direct and indirect questions (¿Cuándo vienes? / No sé cuándo vuelve). Without an accent, cuando = when, joining two clauses (Cuando llego, te llamo).

words.gloss: to keep (doing), to continue; to follow
words.notes: Irregular: sigo, sigue, siguió. seguir + -ndo = to keep doing: sigue lloviendo.
Past: llegué (with -gu-).
doctora = female doctor. Also médico.
Common in Spain; in Latin America carro or auto.
llamarse = to be called: Me llamo Ana = My name is Ana.
más allá = further. Like allí, but less exact.
por última vez = for the last time.
la Tierra = the Earth (the planet).
Me da igual = I don't care. In Spain, igual can mean 'maybe': igual viene.
Also a noun: un loco = a madman.
dar una vuelta = to go for a walk or a drive. de vuelta = back. a la vuelta = on the way back / around the corner.
yo trabajo = I work (trabajo is also the noun 'work, job').
Also a form of jugar: yo juego = I play.
Replaces y before a word that starts with the sound i: padre e hijo.

words.gloss: to go in, to come in, to enter
words.notes: entrar en / a = to go into.
al final = in the end. As an adjective: la parte final = the final part.
estar listo = to be ready. ser listo = to be clever.
Common in Latin America. In Spain: coche.
yo vivo = I live (vivo is also the adjective 'alive').
lo antes posible = as soon as possible.
tener la culpa = to be to blame. Es culpa mía = It's my fault.
Also an adverb: habla más fuerte = speak louder.
Refers to an idea, not a thing: por ello = because of that. More formal than eso.
hacer una pregunta = to ask a question.
¡Atrás! = Get back!
Before a masculine singular noun it becomes mal: un mal día.
el bebé or la bebé, depending on the baby.
As a noun, un segundo = a second (of time).
mi hermano mayor = my older brother. una persona mayor = an elderly person.
In Spain also lunch.
Stem change o → ue; past murió. morirse de hambre = to be starving.

words.gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet
words.notes: Irregular: conozco. conocer = know people and places; saber = know facts.
yo como = I eat (como is also 'like, as'). In Spain, comer also means 'to have lunch'.
tratar de + infinitive = to try to. se trata de = it's about.

words.gloss: to look for; to pick up
words.notes: No preposition: busco mis llaves = I'm looking for my keys. Past: busqué.
The negative of también: Yo tampoco = Me neither.
Stronger than querer. Te amo = I love you (romantic).
Also a noun: un joven = a young man; los jóvenes = young people.
Not the adverb solo (only). Agrees: ella está sola.
un par de = a couple of, a few.
Also 'middle': en medio de = in the middle of. y media = half past.
No tiene sentido = It doesn't make sense.
lejos de = far from.
Feminine, but el arma (stressed a-).
¡Alto! = Stop! en voz alta = out loud.
No te preocupes = Don't worry. Works like gustar: me preocupa = it worries me.
Te doy mi palabra = I give you my word.

words.gloss: to be left, to remain; (quedarse) to stay
words.notes: quedarse = to stay. quedar con alguien = to meet up with someone (Spain).
Often figurative: mi madre me va a matar = my mom will kill me.
ir a la cama = to go to bed.
además de = as well as.
Stem change o → ue: recuerdo. un recuerdo = a memory.
Always acerca de = about.
Plural: luces (z → c).
Stem change o → ue; past durmió. dormirse = to fall asleep.
No hay sitio = There's no room. Mostly Spain; also lugar.
¿Te ayudo? = Can I help you? él ayuda = he helps (ayuda is also the noun 'help').
Like seguir: consigo, consiguió.
More everyday than esposo.

words.gloss: as much as (en cuanto = as soon as)
words.notes: No accent, not a question. cuanto antes = as soon as possible. cuanto más..., más... = the more..., the more...
lo peor = the worst thing.
Also a form of vivir: vivo aquí = I live here.
¡Basta! = That's enough! / Stop it!
los Reyes = the king and queen; also the Three Kings (6 January).
pedir perdón = to apologize. Also a noun: el perdón = forgiveness.

words.gloss: to be missing; to be left (until)
words.notes: Works like gustar: me falta dinero = I'm short of money. hace falta = it's needed.
Stem change e → ie: pierdo. perder el tren = to miss the train.
Used to address a young woman, or a teacher.

words.gloss: to take, to carry; to wear
words.notes: llevar + time = to have been (llevo un año aquí).
¿Tienes fuego? = Have you got a light?
Irregular: pongo, puse, puesto. ponerse = to put on (clothes); to become.

words.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
words.notes: acabar de + infinitive = to have just done: acabo de llegar = I've just arrived.
Also 'royal': la familia real = the royal family.
la orden = an order, a command; el orden = order, tidiness.
Stem change e → ie: empiezo. Past: empecé.
Common in Latin America; in Spain usually fuera.
Also a term of endearment: mi cielo = my darling.
¡Buen viaje! = Have a good trip!
detrás de = behind.
y cuarto = quarter past. Also the ordinal 'fourth'.

words.gloss: free (not busy, not taken; at liberty)
words.notes: Free = no cost is gratis.
No accent, not a question: lo cual = which (referring to a whole idea).
Stem change o → ue. Me suena = It sounds familiar.
Stem change u → ue: yo juego (juego is also the noun 'game'). For music: tocar.
en cambio = on the other hand. a cambio = in exchange.
un millón de + noun: un millón de dólares.
Also a form of extrañar: te extraño = I miss you.
presidenta = female president.
Singular in Spanish: la ropa está sucia = the clothes are dirty.
el agente / la agente.
Usually singular: much information = mucha información.
en general = in general, generally. Also a noun: el general = the general.
¡Trato hecho! = It's a deal!
tener derecho a = to have the right to. As an adjective: right (side); straight.
de todos modos = anyway.
Usually lo demás (everything else) or los demás (the other people).
Plural noticias = news. ¿Qué noticias hay? = What's the news?

sentences.text: Es el coche de mi padre.

sentences.translation: I want a glass of water.

sentences.text: Tengo un perro y un gato.
sentences.translation: I have a dog and a cat.

sentences.text: El libro está en la mesa.
sentences.translation: The book is on the table.
I'll send it to you by mail.
I don't know what to do.

sentences.text: Ella se mira en el espejo.
sentences.translation: She looks at herself in the mirror.
I don't know if he's coming.

sentences.text: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.
sentences.translation: If it rains, I'll stay home.

sentences.text: Es caro, pero es muy bueno.
sentences.translation: It's expensive, but it's very good.
I want to go, but I can't.
Yesterday I went to the doctor.
I want to go with you.
Do you want something to eat?
Do you know anything about her?
When I was a child, I lived here.
I like it when it rains.
How do you get to work?
How do you say "gracias" in English?
I don't know how to do it.

sentences.text: Llego en dos o tres días.
sentences.translation: I'll arrive in two or three days.

sentences.text: Hablo con ella todos los días.
sentences.translation: I talk to her every day.

sentences.text: Esta noche hago yo la cena.

sentences.translation: I'm not coming because I'm sick.
I do it because I love you.
I think it's going to rain.

sentences.text: Si no quieres, entonces me voy.
sentences.translation: If you don't want to, then I'm leaving.
Say hi to him for me.

sentences.text: Los domingos me quedo en casa.

sentences.translation: I don't know who he is.

sentences.text: Hace mucho tiempo que no te veo.
sentences.translation: I haven't seen you in a long time.
I don't know where it is.
Can you do me a favor?
I owe you a lot of favors.
Who is that man over there?

sentences.text: El libro está sobre la mesa.
sentences.translation: The book is on the table.
I don't know anything about him.
I think about you a lot.
We're going to watch a movie.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo era un hombre muy alto.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was a very tall man.

sentences.text: Hay dos hombres en la puerta.
sentences.translation: There are two men at the door.

sentences.text: Es el amor de mi vida.
sentences.translation: He's the love of my life.
I need to talk to someone.
I have to tell you something.
There are many things to do.

sentences.text: Mis cosas están en el coche.
sentences.translation: My things are in the car.

sentences.text: Vamos a ser amigos para siempre.
sentences.translation: We're going to be friends forever.
We went as far as the river.

sentences.text: Vivo aquí desde hace un año.
sentences.translation: I've lived here for a year.

sentences.text: Lávate las manos antes de comer.

sentences.translation: I used to live in Lima.

sentences.text: ¿Por qué no me lo dijiste antes?
sentences.translation: Why didn't you tell me before?
I don't have a single euro.
There are only a few days left.
It was a very long day.

sentences.text: No dormí en toda la noche.

sentences.translation: I have other things to do.
I have a lot of work.
I go to work by bus.
He seemed like a good man.
There are a lot of people here.
He looked at me and smiled.
It's the same people as always.

sentences.text: No se lo digas a nadie.
Pasamos el verano en la playa.
sentences.translation: We spent the summer at the beach.
Can you pass me the salt?

sentences.text: Después de cenar, vemos la tele.

sentences.translation: First we eat and then we talk.

sentences.text: Desde aquí se ve el mar.
sentences.translation: You can see the sea from here.
How much money do you need?

sentences.text: El dinero no lo es todo.

sentences.translation: I want to travel around the world.

sentences.text: Es el mejor café del mundo.
sentences.translation: It's the best coffee in the world.

sentences.text: Me levanto a las siete de la mañana.
sentences.translation: I get up at seven in the morning.
This morning I went to the doctor.

sentences.text: Es la madre de mis hijos.
sentences.translation: She's the mother of my children.

sentences.text: Antes esta casa valía mucho más.
sentences.translation: This house used to be worth much more.
I'm looking for a place to live.
There are very nice places here.

sentences.text: Esta es la casa donde vivo.
sentences.translation: This is the house where I live.

sentences.text: Es el café donde nos conocimos.
sentences.translation: It's the café where we met.
What kind of music do you like?
There are two kinds of people.
I'm going out with my friends.

sentences.text: Nuestros hijos están en la escuela.
Mi mujer trabaja en un hospital.
sentences.translation: My wife works in a hospital.

sentences.text: Hay tres mujeres en la foto.
sentences.translation: There are three women in the photo.

sentences.text: Voy a llamar a mi mamá.
sentences.translation: I'm going to call my mom.
I can't now, we'll talk later.

sentences.text: Cenamos y luego vimos una película.
sentences.translation: We had dinner and then watched a movie.
First I study and then I go out.
I'll be back in three days.
Hey, do you have a minute?
I'd like to go with you.

sentences.text: La mejor parte es el final.
sentences.translation: The best part is the end.
How much do I owe you?
I don't really know what happened.
You matter a lot to me.
Do you mind if I sit down?
I don't care about his problems.
I have so many things to do.
Are you coming to the party?
I have a lot of ideas.
We have a lot of problems.
I've been here for two hours.
By the way, how is your mother?
It was she who called me.

sentences.text: Él es el chico con quien salgo.
sentences.translation: He's the boy I go out with.
There are people who don't eat meat.
He did it all for love.

sentences.text: Está entre la casa y el río.
sentences.translation: It's between the house and the river.
Between us, I don't like it.
Two police officers are talking to him.

sentences.text: Las chicas están en el parque.
sentences.translation: The girls are in the park.

sentences.text: Tengo una cuenta en el banco.
sentences.translation: I have an account at the bank.
We have to pay the bills.

sentences.text: El tren sale a las ocho.

sentences.translation: Do you have brothers or sisters?

sentences.text: Mi hermana es mayor que yo.
sentences.translation: My sister is older than me.
I'm going to think about it.

sentences.text: Dos cabezas piensan mejor que una.
sentences.translation: Two heads are better than one.

sentences.text: Cualquier cosa es mejor que esto.

sentences.translation: I live next to the park.

sentences.text: Hay árboles a los dos lados.
sentences.translation: There are trees on both sides.
There are many cases like this.

sentences.text: ¿No quieres? Pues me lo como yo.
sentences.translation: You don't want it? Then I'll eat it.

sentences.text: Hay cinco personas en la casa.
sentences.translation: There are five people in the house.

sentences.text: Eres la persona más importante para mí.
sentences.translation: You're the most important person to me.

sentences.text: Pon la mesa contra la pared.
sentences.translation: Put the table against the wall.

sentences.text: Todos los caminos llevan a Roma.

sentences.translation: I lived there for ten years.
There are many ways to do it.
I asked a neighbor for help.

sentences.text: Me gusta la historia de España.
sentences.translation: I like the history of Spain.
My grandfather knows a lot of stories.
I'll be back in an hour.
You mean a lot to me.

sentences.text: Trabajo cinco días a la semana.
sentences.translation: I work five days a week.

sentences.text: Hace dos semanas que no la veo.
sentences.translation: I haven't seen her for two weeks.
